content: Each entry includes the title, authors, publication details, and a note indicating that the study design was deemed ineligible for a specific purpose. 1. The study titled Man Papillomavirus Vaccines into Developing Countries International Strategies for Funding and Procurement was published in the journal Vaccine in 2008. However, the study design was deemed ineligible for inclusion in the analysis. 2. Anell A and Persson U explored the role of health-economic evaluations in decision-making for pharmaceutical reimbursement and clinical guidance in Sweden. Their findings were published in European Journal of Health Economics in 2005, but the study design was not eligible for further consideration. 3. Anggriani Y, Ibrahim MIM, Suryawati S, and Shafie AA examined the impact of Indonesia's generic medicine pricing policy on drug prices. Their work appeared in the Journal of Generic Medicines in 2013, but the study design was excluded from eligibility. 4. Annemans L proposed a framework for value-informed and affordable pricing for innovative medicines in the Journal of Medical Economics in 2019. However, the study design was not eligible for inclusion. 5. An anonymous report in the Canadian Pharmacists Journal (2008) highlighted economic threats posed by generic price controls in Newfoundland and Labrador. The study design was deemed ineligible. 6. Abstracts from the 3rd International PPRI Conference in 2015 discussed challenges in pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement policies beyond the financial crisis. These were published in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice, but the study design was not eligible. 7. The AMCP Partnership Forum addressed biosimilars' readiness for market launch in a 2016 publication in the Journal of Managed Care & Specialty Pharmacy. The study design was excluded from eligibility. 8. Another AMCP Partnership Forum in 2017 focused on advancing value-based contracting, as published in the Journal of Managed Care & Specialty Pharmacy. This study design was also ineligible. 9. Ansaripour A, Franken M, Uyl-de Groot C, Kalo Z, and Redekop WK questioned whether external reference pricing threatens international affordability in their 2016 study in Value in Health. The study design was not eligible. 10. Antonanzas F, Oliva J, Pinillos M, and Juarez C analyzed the economic implications of new Spanish pharmaceutical laws in the European Journal of Health Economics in 2007. The study design was deemed ineligible. 11. Arinaminpathy N, Cordier-Lassalle T, Lunte K, and Dye C evaluated the Global Drug Facility's role in the tuberculosis drug market in a 2015 article in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. The study design was excluded. 12. Ashigbie PG, Azameti D, and Wirtz VJ conducted a qualitative study on medicine management challenges under Ghana's National Health Insurance Scheme, published in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice in 2016. The study design was not eligible. 13. Austvoll-Dahlgren A, Aaserud M, Vist G, Ramsay C, Oxman AD, Sturm H, et al. reviewed the effects of cap and co-payment policies on rational drug use in a Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2008. The study design was excluded. 14. Avdi E examined the impact of pricing policies and cost-containment measures in Albania's health insurance scheme in the Romanian Economic and Business Review in 2013. The study design was not eligible. 15. Azzopardi-Muscat N, Schroder-Back P, and Brand H assessed the European Union's Joint Procurement Agreement for cross-border health threats in Health Economics, Policy, and Law in 2017. The study design was excluded. 16. Babar ZU, Kan SW, and Scahill S reviewed interventions promoting the acceptance and uptake of generic medicines in Health Policy in 2014. The study design was not eligible. 17. Bach PB and Pearson SD outlined steps for payers and policymakers to support value-based drug pricing in a 2015 article in JAMA. The study design was excluded. 18. Bae EY, Hong JM, Kwon HY, Jang S, Lee HJ, Bae S, et al. shared South Korea's eight-year experience using health technology assessments for drug reimbursement in Health Policy in 2016. The study design was not eligible. 19. Baker BK discussed patents, pricing, and access to essential medicines in developing countries in a 2009 article in Virtual Mentor. The study design was excluded. 20. Baldwin P analyzed the debate on prescription drug cost-containment and its outcomes in Consultant Pharmacist in 2018. The study design was not eligible. 21. Balotsky ER explored the intersection of strategy and ethics in pharmaceutical pricing policies for Medicare Part D beneficiaries in the Journal of Business Ethics in 2009. The study design was excluded. 22. Bardey D, Bommier A, and Jullien B investigated the relationship between retail price regulation and innovation in the pharmaceutical industry in Journal of Health Economics in 2010. The study design was not eligible. 23. Barla S reported on the slow progress of value purchasing programs and the challenges faced by drug manufacturers in P&T in 2016. The study design was excluded. 24. Barla S also highlighted hurdles to biosimilar acceptance and the lack of competition keeping prices high in a 2016 article in P&T. The study design was not eligible. 25. Barth J, Hammerschmidt T, Vollmar J, Bierbaum M, and Schoffski O analyzed the effects of European reference pricing for vaccines in Germany in Gesundheitswesen in 2014. The study design was excluded. 26. Bastani P, Imanieh MH, Dorosti H, Abbasi R, Dashti SA, and Keshavarz K shared lessons from one year of pooled pharmaceutical procurement in DARU in 2018. The study design was not eligible. 27. Baulinet C, Duraffourg M, and Vanackere S examined specific fiscal policies for health products and their manufacturing industry in a 2012 report. The study design was excluded. 28. Beall RF, Kuhn R, and Attaran A found that compulsory licensing often failed to lower antiretroviral prices compared to international procurement in Health Affairs in 2015. The study design was not eligible. 29. Becker B, Kruppert S, and Kostev K compared economic prescribing of corticosteroid nasal sprays in Germany in International Journal of Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics in 2013. The study design was excluded. 30. Bennie M, Godman B, Bishop I, and Campbell S described initiatives to enhance prescribing efficiency for proton pump inhibitors and statins in Scotland in Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research in 2012. The study design was not eligible.
